texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 1. Purpose
texts.text: 1. Purpose

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This document describes how the Operations team handles inbound customer enquiries received via email, web form, or shared inbox. It is the source of truth for routing, prioritisation, and first-response drafting. All new starters in the dispatch team must follow this SOP.
texts.text: This document describes how the Operations team handles inbound customer enquiries received via email, web form, or shared inbox. It is the source of truth for routing, prioritisation, and first-response drafting. All new starters in the dispatch team must follow this SOP.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 2. Categories
texts.text: 2. Categories

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Every inbound message must be classified into exactly one of the following:
texts.text: Every inbound message must be classified into exactly one of the following:

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Notes on classification:
texts.text: Notes on classification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · If a message contains both a complaint and a new request, classify as COMPLAINT and note the secondary request in the reasoning.
texts.text: If a message contains both a complaint and a new request, classify as COMPLAINT and note the secondary request in the reasoning.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · A request to reschedule an existing booking is a BOOKING , not a complaint, unless the customer explicitly expresses dissatisfaction.
texts.text: A request to reschedule an existing booking is a BOOKING , not a complaint, unless the customer explicitly expresses dissatisfaction.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · If unsure between QUOTE and BOOKING, default to QUOTE - it's safer to confirm scope before dispatching a tradesperson.
texts.text: If unsure between QUOTE and BOOKING, default to QUOTE - it's safer to confirm scope before dispatching a tradesperson.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 3. Priority levels
texts.text: 3. Priority levels

texts.label: text
texts.orig: EMERGENCY messages are always P1. Do not downgrade them, even if the customer's tone is calm.
texts.text: EMERGENCY messages are always P1. Do not downgrade them, even if the customer's tone is calm.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 4. Routing
texts.text: 4. Routing

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Northwind has four operational teams. Route based on category and trade:
texts.text: Northwind has four operational teams. Route based on category and trade:

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Special routing rules:
texts.text: Special routing rules:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · OUT_OF_SCOPE messages route to Customer Care, who send a polite decline.
texts.text: OUT_OF_SCOPE messages route to Customer Care, who send a polite decline.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · If a COMPLAINT involves a billing dispute over $500, it goes to Accounts and Customer Care (cc both).
texts.text: If a COMPLAINT involves a billing dispute over $500, it goes to Accounts and Customer Care (cc both).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Emergency plumbing and emergency electrical both go to Dispatch - we have on-call tradies for both.
texts.text: Emergency plumbing and emergency electrical both go to Dispatch - we have on-call tradies for both.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · We do not have on-call HVAC. After-hours HVAC issues are P2 and route to Dispatch for next-business-day allocation.
texts.text: We do not have on-call HVAC. After-hours HVAC issues are P2 and route to Dispatch for next-business-day allocation.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5. First-response drafting
texts.text: 5. First-response drafting

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Every inbound message gets a first response drafted at triage time, even if a human will edit it before sending. The draft must:
texts.text: Every inbound message gets a first response drafted at triage time, even if a human will edit it before sending. The draft must:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Acknowledge the customer's specific situation in the first sentence.
texts.text: Acknowledge the customer's specific situation in the first sentence.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · State what happens next and roughly when (use the SLA, don't promise a specific time).
texts.text: State what happens next and roughly when (use the SLA, don't promise a specific time).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Match the tone defined in the Tone & Style Guide.
texts.text: Match the tone defined in the Tone & Style Guide.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Never quote a price unless the catalogue lists a fixed price for that exact service.
texts.text: Never quote a price unless the catalogue lists a fixed price for that exact service.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Never commit to a specific tradesperson by name.
texts.text: Never commit to a specific tradesperson by name.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 6. When to flag for human review
texts.text: 6. When to flag for human review

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Mark needs_human_review = true if any of the following apply:
texts.text: Mark needs_human_review = true if any of the following apply:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · The customer is angry, distressed, or threatens legal action / online review.
texts.text: The customer is angry, distressed, or threatens legal action / online review.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · The request involves a quote over $5,000 or a refund over $500.
texts.text: The request involves a quote over $5,000 or a refund over $500.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · The message is in a language other than English, or appears garbled.
texts.text: The message is in a language other than English, or appears garbled.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · You cannot confidently classify the message after re-reading it.
texts.text: You cannot confidently classify the message after re-reading it.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · The customer mentions a previous complaint or escalation.
texts.text: The customer mentions a previous complaint or escalation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · The request is for a service that is borderline outside our catalogue.
texts.text: The request is for a service that is borderline outside our catalogue.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Flagging is cheap. Missing an escalation is expensive. When in doubt, flag.
texts.text: Flagging is cheap. Missing an escalation is expensive. When in doubt, flag.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7. Out-of-hours handling
texts.text: 7. Out-of-hours handling

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Outside 7:00-18:00 weekdays, only P1 EMERGENCY messages are actioned live. P2 and P3 are queued for the next business morning. The first-response draft for queued messages should acknowledge the wait time ("we'll be in touch first thing tomorrow") rather than promising same-day action.
texts.text: Outside 7:00-18:00 weekdays, only P1 EMERGENCY messages are actioned live. P2 and P3 are queued for the next business morning. The first-response draft for queued messages should acknowledge the wait time ("we'll be in touch first thing tomorrow") rather than promising same-day action.

Customer has an active risk to property or safety: water leak in progress, no hot water in winter, electrical sparking, gas smell, etc.
Customer is asking about an invoice, payment, refund, or account statement.
The request is for something we don't offer, or is not actionable (spam, wrong number, etc.).

table_cells.text: All BOOKING and EMERGENCY messages. They allocate the right tradesperson and call the customer back.
All QUOTE messages. They send written estimates and follow up.
All BILLING messages. They handle invoices, payments, and refunds.
All COMPLAINT messages. They are also the fallback for anything that doesn't fit cleanly elsewhere.
